name: Museum St. Johann in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum St. Johann in Tirol: regional history, alpinism on the Wilder Kaiser, Artothek gallery, and geology of the Kitzbühel Alps.
beschreibung:
Overview

The modern Museum St. Johann in Tirol is located in the historic market center of the vibrant municipality of St. Johann in Tirol (Kitzbühel district) at Dechant-Wieshofer-Straße 2, at an altitude of approximately 660 meters. Framed by the striking rock massif of the Wilder Kaiser and the Kitzbüheler Horn, the cultural center, founded in 1993, is housed in the former elementary school. Awarded the renowned Austrian Museum Seal of Quality, the house brings together a multifaceted local history and mining museum, the Alpine Museum Wilder Kaiser, and a contemporary art gallery under one roof.

Route & Requirements

The museum spans a fascinating arc from the first prehistoric settlement traces of the Bronze Age to the modern sports and tourism history of the Leukental valley. A major focus illuminates the heyday of mining on the Rerobichl in the 16th and 17th centuries: with the deepest shaft in the world at that time (the Heilig-Geist-Schacht with almost 900 meters depth), St. Johann was a European center for copper and silver extraction.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum St. Johann in Tirol is open from Tuesday to Saturday from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM and from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM (closed on Sundays, Mondays, and public holidays; seasonal break in May and November). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and teenagers (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.50, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €11.00. Holders of the regional St. Johann Card receive free admission! Arrival by train: St. Johann in Tirol is an important express train stop on the ÖBB (Giselabahn); from the station, it's just about a five-minute walk through the pedestrian zone directly to the museum. By car: Via the B178 (Loferer Straße) or B161 directly to St. Johann, parking is available in the town center (Parkgarage Zentrum or Tiefgarage Post).

Tips

The museum is barrier-free and wheelchair-accessible via an external ramp and a passenger elevator. For children, there is an interactive museum quiz that playfully guides them through the exhibition rooms. Combine your museum visit with a stroll across St. Johann's baroque main square and visit the magnificent Deanery Church of Maria Himmelfahrt with its ceiling frescoes by Simon Benedikt Faistenberger. In the immediate vicinity, you will also find numerous shopping opportunities and restaurants to round off your visit. Allow ample time to explore the diverse exhibits and the art gallery at your leisure.
